metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Great Bend, Susquehanna County? Dry-gas Marcellus territory along the Susquehanna River's namesake bend. We buy — no pressure to sell.
heroLead: Great Bend sits at the sweeping oxbow the Susquehanna River carves near the New York line, an old railroad town now sitting on some of the state's most productive dry-gas acreage.
intro: Great Bend is a Susquehanna County borough named for the dramatic bend the Susquehanna River makes as it curves back toward New York, historically an Erie Railroad junction town. Today the surrounding farmland sits within one of the most heavily developed parts of the dry-gas Marcellus play, led for years by Cabot Oil & Gas, now Coterra Energy.
We buy mineral and royalty interests near Great Bend, whether your family's acreage is producing, leased and quiet, or split among several heirs.

sections.heading: A railroad town over strong dry-gas rock
paragraphs: Great Bend's history as a rail junction shaped its early development, but the mineral story here is really about what's underneath the surrounding farmland — some of the most consistently developed dry-gas Marcellus acreage in the state.

sections.heading: What sustained development means for owners
paragraphs: Because this area has been developed for well over a decade, most Great Bend-area interests have meaningful production history to evaluate, which gives a clearer basis for valuation than newer or undeveloped acreage.

sections.heading: Our review process
paragraphs: We look at lease terms, production trend, and current royalty statement deductions before naming an offer, and explain our reasoning clearly.
We're happy to walk through exactly how a unit's production history translated into the number we offer.

faqs.question: Why is Great Bend named that way?
faqs.answer: It refers to the sharp bend the Susquehanna River makes as it curves near the New York state line — a geographic feature, not related to mineral rights, though it's how the borough got its name.

faqs.question: Has Cabot Oil & Gas been active near Great Bend?
faqs.answer: Yes, Cabot, now Coterra Energy, has been the dominant operator developing dry-gas Marcellus acreage across Susquehanna County, including this area, for well over a decade.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests split among multiple heirs near Great Bend?
faqs.answer: Yes, fractional interests inherited by multiple family members are common on Susquehanna County farmland, and we regularly buy an individual heir's share.

faqs.question: Does the Erie Railroad history around Great Bend show up in mineral deed records?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, in older right-of-way and easement language on parcels near the former rail corridor, though this generally affects surface use rather than the oil and gas mineral interest itself.
